lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' quiet offseason has a sharp little edge to it now - Gavin McKenna is already forcing a conversation, and the club's choice to keep him off the top power-play unit says the coaches want patience, not theater. That handling of McKenna after his first pro taste is the week's telling development; he looked dangerous enough to matter, while Auston Matthews said he's shaken off the rust after the preseason opener. Toronto's finished season is behind it, so the only record that matters now is the roster ledger, and that one is still being written. The real question is how quickly McKenna's skill can be folded into a lineup that already has Matthews, William Nylander and John Tavares demanding puck time. Watch camp for the power-play pecking order - and for whether McKenna stays sheltered or gets thrown into the fire.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season has already slid out of reach, and now Toronto is left staring at the wreckage and the repair bill. Trey Yesavage is set to start Monday against the Orioles - a reminder that the Blue Jays are already sorting out arms for the next chapter, not the next pennant push. The club sits at 76-79, three games out of the final wild card, but that number now matters only as a frame for what comes next. Spencer Miles is getting another turn, the bullpen has been leaned on hard, and the roster is being treated like a live audition. Yesavage's return after knee trouble gives the front office one more look at a young arm with real relevance. What matters now is how Toronto shapes this rotation, and whether it finds enough health and certainty before camp opens again.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet can be revealing in this business - and Toronto's silence is speaking loudest through ceremony. Kyle Lowry's weekend of honors, capped by the city key and the statue reveal, gave the franchise a clean template for how it should treat its legends; that matters because the Raptors are deep in the offseason and the only score that counts now is how well they manage the next chapter. The club's 46-36 finish and 5th in the East are history, not a destination. What matters is the roster's shape around Kawhi Leonard's return and the way the organization balances nostalgia with hard edges. DeMar DeRozan's presence at the Lowry celebration was no accident - Toronto still has its old heart. Training camp will tell whether this team is a reunion act or a contender with teeth.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The early noise around Washington is all about what survives the cut and what blossoms under the new spotlight. Chig Okonkwo's hamstring injury has opened the door for Ben Sinnott, with John Bates also set for a larger slice of the tight end pie - the kind of roster turn that tells you where the staff's trust really lives. Antonio Williams has already lit a fuse with his debut, while Tyler Owens has the fan base buzzing for the right reasons: energy, violence, and a knack for special teams work that coaches notice fast. Mike Sainristil, meanwhile, remains the sort of corner whose assignment can swing a whole afternoon. Washington is in the offseason now, with the roster still being sorted. Watch Sinnott's role, the secondary's shape, and whether these young pieces force the front office's hand before camp hardens the depth chart.

article.title: Sunday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs are in the thick of camp talk, with a fresh debate over whether McKenna should be put next to Matthews right away, while Matthews says he has shaken off the rust after the preseason opener. For the Blue Jays, the mood is harsher after another painful loss pushed them further back in the wild-card race, and the morning papers are already calling it another must-win missed. The Raptors are still deep in offseason mode, with a draft awards piece and a note that Lowry's celebration offered a clean template for honoring team legends.

The Commanders have their own September focus, with Dallas next on the list and a close look ahead at what Ben Sinnott can do without Chig Okonkwo in the picture. For a Toronto fan with one eye on Washington, that is enough to fill the coffee break, especially with the Leafs still sorting combinations and the Jays trying to steady the season before the calendar turns.
